lbHelp: Takes effect with multiple backends. A backend can be written as {example}; adding {backup} enables it only when all other backends are unavailable
timeoutsHelp: 0 uses the default: 10 seconds to connect and for the TLS handshake, no limit on waiting for response headers. The wait for response headers starts once the request is sent and does not affect later downloads or long-lived connections such as WebSocket and SSE; a timeout returns 504
healthHelp: When disabled, passive ejection still applies: a backend with 3 consecutive connection failures is paused for 30 seconds
cacheHelp: Only caches GET requests without cookies or authorization headers; honors upstream Cache-Control by default and can be set per path
ttlHelp: Seconds; used when the upstream declares no caching. 0 caches only responses the upstream explicitly allows
cacheRulesHelp: Without *, matches by path prefix (/api matches /api and /api/x); with *, matches the whole path and * can span /. More specific paths win; unmatched paths use the defaults above. Cache: honors the backend's Cache-Control and uses the duration when the backend declares none. Force cache: ignores the backend's Cache-Control and caches for the duration, but responses with Set-Cookie are still never cached. Duration 0 uses the default duration. To cache only specific paths, set / to don't cache
clientTimeoutsHelp: 0 uses the default of 60 seconds. Only a single read or write that stalls is timed, so uploads and downloads that keep moving, waiting for the backend and long-lived connections such as WebSocket are not affected; it drops visitors that send or read extremely slowly, and a request body timeout returns 408
compressHelp: Enable br / gzip for text responses (responses already compressed by the backend are not compressed again)
maxConnsHelp: Requests handled at the same time per IP; 0 means unlimited
rewriteHelp: Matched in order; the first match stops processing. A rewritten path is sent to the backend, and redirects keep the query parameters
